transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. —. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just keep making these really dumb mistakes at work. I supervise a sales team, and lately I'm messing up our sales reports. Like, I'll copy the wrong numbers over from the team dashboard, or I'll completely miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check. 

It's frustrating because it happens even when I thought I already went over it and checked my work. I just need to figure out why I keep doing this.
Before these work problems, did you have similar difficulty paying attention or making careless mistakes when you were a child?

Yeah, I was... I was actually like this as a kid, too. My mom still talks about it, to be honest. She brings up these notes my teachers used to send home back in elementary school. They'd always say I rushed through my assignments or lost my homework. And, um, they also said I talked out of turn a lot and just couldn't stay in my seat without being reminded to sit back down. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing.
Do you often feel excessively worried or on edge most days?
No, not really. I mean, I get frustrated with myself about work and all the mistakes, but I wouldn't say I feel worried or on edge most of the time. It's more just annoying than anything else.
Do you also have trouble staying organized or paying attention in other parts of your life, like at home or in social situations?

Yeah, it definitely spills over. At work, it's actually gotten to the point where my manager brought it up in my formal review, which is... not great. And at home, it's a problem too. It just causes arguments because my family feels like they can't count on me to follow through on things I say I'm going to do. So, yeah, it's definitely affecting both areas.
